Let us examine the sequence methodically.

**The Bug:**
The off-by-one error occurs at the initialization boundary of the iteration. By setting the starting index of the `range` function to `1`, the loop systematically bypasses the very first element of the collection, `xs[0]`. Consequently, the final total will be missing this initial value.

**The Fix:**
To ensure the complete and accurate summation of all elements in `xs`, we must adjust the starting index to `0`. The corrected line should be recorded as:
`for i in range(0, len(xs)):` 

*(Note: As a matter of Pythonic housekeeping, simply writing `for i in range(len(xs)):` is also perfectly acceptable, as the default starting index is `0`.)*
